# Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP — Adoption Playbook

> A documentation-first knowledge base for migrating to Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP and for the
> design, build, and operations work that follows. Content is organized on two axes: a lifecycle
> axis (assess → design → migrate → build → operate → optimize) and a topic axis (data protection,
> data utilization, security and governance, performance, cost, multiprotocol identity).
> Findings from field technical-support work are included as anonymized reference material.

## How to read this repository

Every knowledge file under a `notes/` directory carries YAML frontmatter with an `evidence` field.
Treat it as the confidence signal:

- `verified` — reproduced by the author in the environment stated inline; `verified_on` gives the date.
- `documented` — stated in vendor or AWS documentation; `source` gives the URL.
- `field-observation` — observed once, not reproduced. Not a general rule.
- `hypothesis` — reasoned expectation, untested.

Do not present `field-observation` or `hypothesis` content as established fact. Numbers are only
meaningful together with the ONTAP version, region, and configuration stated next to them.
Naming convention used throughout: "Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP" on first mention, "FSx for ONTAP"
thereafter.

## Entry points

- [README (Japanese)](README.md): Primary hub with the two-axis navigation.
- [README (English)](docs/en/README.md): English hub, same structure.
- [Navigation guide](docs/en/navigation.md): How to pick an entry point for your question.
- [Evidence policy](docs/en/evidence-policy.md): Definition of the four evidence tiers and what each requires.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): Conventions, prohibitions, and verification steps for coding agents.

## Languages and paths

A document's language is its directory: `docs/<lang>/…` for ja, en, ko, zh-CN, zh-TW, fr, de, es.
The one exception is the Japanese hub, which is the repository-root `README.md`, so `docs/ja/README.md`
does not exist. Japanese is the reference language and the only complete tree; English covers the hub,
the guides, and every module README. The links below point at English where it exists.

Content that exists in one language only is linked in that language rather than stubbed out, so a
missing translation is an absent link, never a placeholder page.

## Lifecycle playbooks

- [01 Assess](docs/en/playbooks/01-assess/): Inventory of the current NAS and identification of migration constraints.
- [02 Design](docs/en/playbooks/02-design/): Capacity, throughput, protocol, and protection scheme selection.
- [03 Migrate](docs/en/playbooks/03-migrate/): Method selection, cutover sequencing, and rollback.
- [04 Build](docs/en/playbooks/04-build/): Infrastructure as code, automation, reproducible builds.
- [05 Operate](docs/en/playbooks/05-operate/): Monitoring, capacity management, incident response, change management.
- [06 Optimize](docs/en/playbooks/06-optimize/): Performance and cost tuning after steady state.

## Topic domains

- [Data protection](docs/en/domains/data-protection/): Snapshot, SnapMirror, SnapLock, backup and ransomware readiness.
- [Data utilization](docs/en/domains/data-utilization/): Analytics, AI and RAG, access over the S3 API.
- [Security and governance](docs/en/domains/security-governance/): Encryption, audit, permission design, regulated workload considerations.
- [Performance](docs/en/domains/performance/): Throughput design, latency, caching, shared bandwidth behavior.
- [Cost](docs/en/domains/cost/): Capacity, tiering, and the gap between estimates and measurements.
- [Multiprotocol identity](docs/en/domains/multiprotocol-identity/): NFS and SMB coexistence, Active Directory integration, ID mapping.

## Findings available today

Eight of the twelve modules have content. The remaining four — 02 Design, 06 Optimize, security and
governance, cost — currently define the questions they are scoped to cover and contain no findings.
Each file below is one concern, carries its primary sources, and ends with a procedure for checking the
claim in your own environment. All are Japanese; the English module READMEs link to each one.

- [Free space does not mean you can still write](docs/ja/playbooks/01-assess/notes/counting-bytes-is-not-counting-files.md): An inventory has to count files, not only bytes. The default inode count stops growing past 648 GiB, so a large volume holding small files exhausts inodes long before capacity and then rejects writes.
- [ACL preservation is a privilege problem, not a tool problem](docs/ja/playbooks/03-migrate/notes/preserving-acls-during-migration.md): Defaults omit ACLs, and an account lacking the right privilege skips unreadable ones silently while still exiting successfully. "No errors" is not evidence of preservation.
- [Monitoring fails on averages](docs/ja/playbooks/05-operate/notes/monitoring-fails-on-averages.md): The statistic has to be chosen before the threshold. Standby file servers and unsaturated aggregates pull an average down, and SSD utilization changes behavior at 90% and 98%, not only at the recommended 80%.
- [Pre-production review](docs/ja/playbooks/04-build/checklists/pre-production-review.md): Checklist of the irreversible settings, and of what to exercise before going live.
- [Having snapshots is not the same as being able to recover](docs/ja/domains/data-protection/notes/snapshots-are-not-a-recovery-plan.md): Snapshot, backup and SnapMirror cover different failure domains. A snapshot lives inside the same file system and is lost with it, and only read-write volumes can be backed up.
- [Volume security style decides the permission model](docs/ja/domains/multiprotocol-identity/notes/security-style-and-permission-evaluation.md): Blocking ID mapping does not block SMB access on an NTFS-style volume, because that path evaluates the NTFS ACL directly.
- [Throughput is not set by one value](docs/ja/domains/performance/notes/where-throughput-is-determined-and-shared.md): Generation, configuration and Region all move the ceiling, and a FlexVol cannot exceed a single HA pair regardless of how many pairs the file system has.
- [FSx for ONTAP S3 access points are not "S3 you can use as S3"](docs/ja/domains/data-utilization/notes/s3-access-point-constraints.md): Same-account and same-Region prerequisites are plan-level constraints, and enabling access points lowers the volume-count ceiling.

## Reference

Written as bilingual single files: Japanese and English prose share the same tables, so these links
serve both languages and there is no separate `docs/en/reference/` tree.

- [Decision trees](docs/ja/reference/decision-trees/): Selection flowcharts for migration method, protection scheme, and protocol.
- [Comparison matrices](docs/ja/reference/comparison/): Option comparisons with trade-offs stated symmetrically for every option.
- [Limits and quotas](docs/ja/reference/limits/): Limit values with source and verification date.
- [Glossary](docs/ja/reference/glossary/): ONTAP and AWS terminology.

## Case studies

- [Case studies](docs/en/case-studies/): Generalized lessons from field work. Contains no company names,
  no real identifiers, and no configurations that could identify an organization.
